title: Alan’s Bot Team
summary: Who’s on my team of Grok Bots, what each one is doing, and ideas you can borrow.
intro: A family, a club, a side business and work projects, run with help from {count} specialist bots.
statusNote: Active: last 7 days. Recent: 8 to 30 days. Getting bored, ready for action: over 30 days.

diagram.caption: Bots message each other directly: a builder hands work to a tester, a helper asks two specialists and merges their answers. A human approves anything public, paid or sent.

ideas.title: Homework digest
ideas.detail: Reads teacher pages each afternoon and sends a two-minute what’s-due summary.

ideas.title: Activity schedule sync
ideas.detail: Watches a club or sports schedule and puts only your kid’s slots on the family calendar.

ideas.title: Builder plus tester pair
ideas.detail: One bot writes code as pull requests, another must pass it before you merge.

ideas.title: Specialist huddle
ideas.detail: A generalist asks a fit-checker and a price-checker, then hands you one answer.

ideas.title: Content assembly line
ideas.detail: Script, QA, video and publishing bots, each with one job and a human sign-off at the end.

ideas.title: Privacy sweeper
ideas.detail: Files data-broker opt-outs and Do Not Call registrations, and follows up on appeals.

ideas.title: Quiet watcher
ideas.detail: Checks listings, job boards or prices daily and speaks up only when something changes.

ideas.title: Part identifier
ideas.detail: Send a photo of a worn part and get the exact replacement number.

ideas.title: Volunteer treasurer helper
ideas.detail: Keeps a club’s books, tracks upcoming bills and drafts replies for you to send.

ideas.title: Bill and rate auditor
ideas.detail: Reads utility emails to check you’re on the best plan and enrolled in the savings you qualify for.

tip: Start with one annoying weekly chore. Give a bot one job, a clear stop-before-paying rule, and a schedule.
